options.label: Owner-supplied exact local root with one-attempt attestation
options.effect: Bind no path now; later require a separately authorized fresh bounded storage and atomic-capability attestation for an exact local fixed NTFS/ReFS non-cloud root with both 5 GiB and 15 percent free, no reparse path, and no worktree or broadly shared location.
options.tradeoff: Strongest portable and fail-closed policy, but an eligible root still must be provided and separately checked.

options.label: Prefer F drive after cleanup
options.effect: Treat F as the intended root if a future fresh check passes the same thresholds and constraints.
options.tradeoff: Matches the earlier storage preference but creates a machine-specific default and F was historically ineligible.

options.label: Allow owner-owned encrypted removable storage
options.effect: Permit an exact encrypted external SSD after separate attachment, filesystem, capacity, and custody evidence.
options.tradeoff: Adds capacity flexibility but increases device identity, disconnect, custody, and portability risks.

options.label: Defer storage policy
options.effect: Leave root type, thresholds, freshness, and path constraints unresolved.
options.tradeoff: No storage action occurs, but R1 cannot be prepared.

options.label: Defender plus ModelScan plus passive structure inspector
options.effect: Require exact pinned no-remediation Microsoft Defender custom scanning, exact pinned ModelScan static serialization scanning, and an exact bounded framework-free passive structure inspector; every layer must pass.
options.tradeoff: Broadest coverage and auditability, but exact installed versions, binaries, package hashes, and commands still need a separate bounded binding process.

options.label: Defender and passive inspector only
options.effect: Use platform malware scanning and H-CAM structural checks without ModelScan.
options.tradeoff: Fewer dependencies but weaker coverage for known model-serialization risks.

options.label: ModelScan and passive inspector only
options.effect: Use model-specific static scanning and H-CAM structural checks without platform antimalware.
options.tradeoff: Avoids Defender-specific behavior but loses general malware detection.

options.label: Defer scanner chain
options.effect: Leave every scanner product and command unresolved.
options.tradeoff: Avoids an early tool choice but keeps R1 blocked.

options.label: All layers clean, supported, complete, and fail closed
options.effect: Reject any detection, severity finding, unsupported or skipped target, timeout, crash, malformed report, ambiguous Defender result, version drift, missing provenance, or unsafe structure; no manual hard-gate override.
options.tradeoff: Strongest security boundary but can reject legitimate artifacts until evidence or tooling improves.

options.label: Critical and high findings block
options.effect: Permit medium and low findings after review.
options.tradeoff: Reduces false-positive blocking but introduces discretionary exceptions before a trustworthy baseline exists.

options.label: Manual owner override
options.effect: Allow the owner to waive scanner or provenance failures per artifact.
options.tradeoff: Flexible but violates the accepted fail-closed admission policy.

options.label: Informational scans only
options.effect: Record findings without affecting artifact state.
options.tradeoff: Insufficient for R1 supply-chain acceptance.

options.label: Sequential partial-hash-scan-BOM-atomic-seal
options.effect: Acquire one exact allowlisted artifact at a time into an exclusive partial file, enforce size, hash and identity, run all passive scanner layers, produce license/provenance/CycloneDX ML-BOM evidence, then atomically seal accepted or rejected state without automatic deletion.
options.tradeoff: Most auditable and bounded, but slower than parallel acquisition and requires explicit cleanup authority for rejected objects.

options.label: Parallel bounded acquisition
options.effect: Download all three exact objects concurrently before scanning.
options.tradeoff: Faster but increases storage, network, failure-isolation, and evidence-correlation complexity.

options.label: Direct final-name acquisition
options.effect: Write artifacts directly to their final candidate paths and scan afterward.
options.tradeoff: Simpler but exposes incomplete or unverified objects as apparently final.

options.label: Defer acquisition lifecycle
options.effect: Retain source metadata without an acquisition state machine.
options.tradeoff: R1 remains unissuable.

options.label: Immutable R1 passive review before separately authorized R2
options.effect: R1 may only acquire, hash, passively scan, and document supply chain; any checkpoint loading, even weights-only, and all generated calibration require a later exact network-denied R2 authority after R1 acceptance.
options.tradeoff: Strongest isolation and audit trail but requires another explicit gate before learning anything from runtime behavior.

options.label: Allow weights-only load during R1
options.effect: Permit CPU weights-only framework loading after scans to inspect tensors.
options.tradeoff: Earlier compatibility information but crosses the accepted passive R1 boundary and still cannot establish complete safety.

options.label: Combine R1 acquisition and R2 calibration
options.effect: Acquire, load, and run the generated C1 matrix in one authorization.
options.tradeoff: Faster but collapses supply-chain review, runtime activation, and calibration into one blast radius.

options.label: Defer lifecycle separation
options.effect: Leave the boundary between artifact review and runtime execution undefined.
options.tradeoff: Blocks a defensible R1 package.
